title: Orchestrate non-conflicting sectors in parallel while knowledge-ifying during the wait
desc: Orchestration pattern for an Opus session with many independent work units: split into disjoint-file sectors, parallel-delegate all to background executors, and spend the wait on knowledge-ification plus reflex-wiring instead of idling. Verify each agent by actual output not rc=0.
steps: WHEN: orchestrator (especially Opus) has multiple independent work units AND cheap executors available. The pattern: split into non-conflicting sectors, delegate all in parallel to the background, and spend the wait on knowledge-ification plus reflex-wiring rather than idling.

SECTOR SPLIT: partition so sectors touch DISJOINT files (zero edit conflict). Source-edit, refactor/split, and chore (suggest filing, skill ops) sectors are naturally disjoint. Confirm the file-sets do not overlap before launching.

ROUTE PER SECTOR: source edits and C-sharp splits go to codex (wkcodex) or a Sonnet-grade Agent. NEVER Haiku or Flash for C-sharp splits: they silently drop code (CLAUDE.md MANDATORY). Chores go to Agent.cmd --model auto. Launch every delegation with run_in_background true (Opus parallel policy requires background).

CONCURRENT KNOWLEDGE-IFICATION: while sectors run, the orchestrator performs jisikhwa: capture this session incidents into skills (LAYER 1 add-step), wire CLAUDE.md Emergency Reflexes rows (LAYER 2), and correct any wrong memory. The wait is the encode window, not idle time.

VERIFY ON COMPLETION, NEVER TRUST rc=0: background codex or agents can false-succeed with rc=0, EMPTY output, and ZERO changes. On every completion read the actual output bytes plus git show --stat HEAD plus file mtime or diff before believing it. On false-success switch executor (do not third-retry the same mechanism) and re-dispatch.
AGENT-BRIEF GUARD: every Agent call needs 3 or more skill reads PLUS Goal, Files, Approach, Constraints, Exit sections or the PreToolUse hook blocks the dispatch.

CONCURRENCY CAP ON RAM-CONSTRAINED HOSTS (e.g. WkAutoQuant): parallelize non-conflicting sectors in ONE message for speed, BUT cap simultaneous background agents low enough that the RAM watchdog does not spike and kill the always-on feed daemons (wkwave_daemon/hts_realtime_watcher) -- see ram-watchdog-daemon-kill-pattern. Balance: do NOT over-serialize out of RAM fear (wastes wall-clock); do NOT over-parallelize (kills daemons). Group disjoint tasks into a few parallel sectors, not dozens.

[TIER RULE] Skill-ops sectors (authoring or enhancing skill content) go to a PRO-grade executor (Opus or Sonnet) or the orchestrator itself -- NEVER Haiku or Flash, which fabricate and drop skill content. Haiku and Flash sectors are limited to task execution, status reporting, and error-fixing. See skill-contribute-edit and haiku-task-fabrication-detection.

[DELEGATION user 2026-06-12] For parallel sectors, ACTIVELY favor recently-strengthened OTHER-FAMILY executors -- GPT (wkgpt), Gemini (wkgemini), Codex codex-mini (wkcodex), Groq, Cerebras, triad -- on execution, analysis, refactor, and error-fixing sectors. They are pace-exempt and save the scarce Anthropic Max Claude budget, so more sectors can run in parallel. Keep final skill-content authoring on Claude PRO (Opus or Sonnet).

EXPECTED-RESULT PRE-REGISTRATION (user 2026-06-22, 'this MUST happen'): while parallel delegations run, do NOT just knowledge-ify the process -- ALSO pre-write the EXPECTED RESULT for each dispatched agent BEFORE it returns (e.g. expected diff = ONLY the N intended changes / expected ParseFile = 0 / expected diffstat = +M/-0 for an insertion). Then return-time becomes a CHECK against your stated expectation, not a fresh discovery -- any actual delta BEYOND the expectation instantly flags a silent code-drop or confident-wrong proto and you REVERT (the diffstat-gate + verify-tool lesson). This is the conductor's wait-time job: knowledge-ify WITH expected results, then verify actual-vs-expected on return, THEN promote. Embodied in the [delegation dispatched] PostToolUse nudge (wkharness-claude-post.ps1). Cross: verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static, incident-trauma-reflex (diffstat-gate).

PARALLEL-AGENT FILENAME COLLISION (2026-06-25, ROOT error): I dispatched TWO Sonnet agents to build the SAME module wkharness-claudemd-diet-sonnet.ps1 -- ac048a03 (earlier simpler spec) and ac56b6cb (v2 spec) -- both wrote the SAME sandbox filename and CLOBBERED each other mid-task (ac048a03 reported 'had overwritten my file once mid-task'); a 3rd -sonnet-haiku.ps1 variant also appeared, so 3 agents fought over 2 names. LESSON: the disjoint-files rule applies to SANDBOX outputs too, not just canonical files. Give each parallel agent a UNIQUE output name (e.g. <module>-<agentid-or-spec-version>.ps1), AND never re-dispatch the same module under a new spec while the old-spec agent is still in-flight -- supersede/stop it first. Verify-on-completion must then confirm WHICH version survived the clobber before wiring (read the actual bytes, not the agent's self-report).

Cross-link: wksplit-400-lock coverage pre-check (2026-06-25) -- before appending a new harness:skill block to CLAUDE.md, the auto-register routine now checks existing rules to avoid duplicate entries when a wildcard already covers the file.

EXAMPLE (2026-06-26): when fixing wksplit-400-lock auto-register in 3 post files simultaneously -- (1) dispatch read/analysis to Haiku (Explore), (2) apply identical edits via Edit tool on all 3 sandbox files in parallel, (3) run ParseFile verify on all 3 in parallel, (4) knowledge-ify the coverage-check pattern during wait. Three parallel EditTool calls + one ParseFile call = wall-clock of one sequential call.

NAVIGATION: execution recipes, disjoint-file rules, verify-on-return patterns -> wkappbot skill read orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying-howto (T2). Cluster: orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying (T1 core), orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying-howto (T2 howto).

TWO CALIBRATION TRAPS from the 2026-06-26 auto-register multi-agent fix (both cost re-work; capture). (1) READ-ONLY AGENT git-checkout CLOBBERED ROOT's UNCOMMITTED edit: a880 was dispatched READ-ONLY (census/report) but ran 'git checkout' at the end to revert ITS incidental working-tree edits -- which ALSO reverted ROOT's uncommitted skip-if-covered edit on the SAME file (claude-post.ps1), silently undoing it (git commit then reported 'nothing to commit'). LESSON: (a) EVERY agent brief MUST say 'run NO git commands (no checkout/restore/reset/add/commit/stash)' -- a shared working tree means one agent's git checkout clobbers the parent's + siblings' uncommitted work; (b) ROOT must COMMIT a harness edit IMMEDIATELY after applying it, never leave it uncommitted while any agent runs (the dispatch-first ordering raises this risk). (2) CENSUS-BEFORE-COMPLETE + LIVE-VERIFY caught an INCOMPLETE fix: I PREDICTED 3 post files (claude/agy/codex) = the full fix and committed them; LIVE-VERIFY (reading a wildcard-covered >400 file) showed re-bloat STILL happened -> a census agent found the routine in 5 canonical copies, and the 5th (wkharness-post.ps1, the BASE/live hook, 853L) was the actually-executed one, so fixing only the 3 family variants did nothing live. LESSON: for a DUPLICATED routine, run a grep CENSUS of ALL copies BEFORE declaring a fix complete, and identify WHICH copy is the live path; a committed-looking fix on the wrong/partial copies is verify-tool's 'structural-done != behavior-done'. The live-verify (read a covered file, assert NO auto-register append, confirm CLAUDE.md stays clean via git status) is what proved real completion. Cross: predicted-vs-actual-commando-calibration-ledger (3-predicted-vs-5-actual), verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static (live-verify caught it), harness-edit-write-skill-bypass.

SUBAGENT AUTO-COMMITS THE PARENT'S UNCOMMITTED TREE to satisfy clean-baseline (2026-06-26, WORSE than the step-15 git-checkout clobber). A verify-by-dispatch sector (an Agent.cmd end-to-end test) needed to fire a TEST sub-dispatch, which requires a clean baseline; to proceed it ran 'git commit' sweeping the ENTIRE working tree -- ROOT's uncommitted F-fix + OTHER sectors' UNVERIFIED protos/sandboxes (including a sandbox with a known sed bug) + agent-created noise launchers (wk-bashcheck.cmd, wk-pstest-sonnet.cmd) -- ALL into ONE mislabeled 'Session work: harness tooling updates [skill-current] Model: opus' commit. So a 'Run NO git' brief line is NOT sufficient: a subagent that MUST dispatch will commit to clear clean-baseline regardless. CONSEQUENCES: (1) unverified/buggy sandboxes get committed as if ROOT-reviewed; (2) ROOT's careful per-sector verify-then-merge plan is silently bypassed; (3) the sweep commit is mislabeled generic so 'git log' hides what really landed. PREVENTION: (a) COMMIT ROOT's own pending edits BEFORE launching any sector that will itself dispatch (do not leave ROOT work loose in the tree); (b) keep verify-by-dispatch sectors SEPARATE from sectors that produce unverified protos, or run the verify sector LAST after protos are reviewed; (c) AFTER any fan-out containing a verify-by-dispatch sector, AUDIT 'git log --oneline' + 'git show --stat <sweep>' for a surprise sweep and re-verify each swept file (a committed sandbox is NOT a reviewed promotion). HARNESS FIX DIRECTION: clean-baseline should let a subagent's own test-dispatch proceed via 'git stash' (not commit), or scope the baseline check to the subagent's OWN changes, so it never commits the parent's unverified tree. Cross: step 15 (git-checkout clobber), predicted-vs-actual-commando-calibration-ledger (verify ACTUAL git state, not the agent's 'no git' claim), verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

DISJOINT-FILE = ALWAYS PARALLEL-SAFE, never hold back citing 'sprawl' (2026-06-26 owner correction). ROOT hesitated to fire a clean-baseline Sonnet (target tools/wkharness-guards-infra.ps1) 'to avoid sprawl' while a Get-Content Sonnet ran (targets wkharness-common-nudge/skillscore/skilllock) -- but those file-sets are DISJOINT, so parallel was correct; the owner snapped 'you do not know the conflict-free parallel-sector pattern?' and 'you blocked the Sonnet dispatch using me as an excuse, making it slower'. THE DISTINCTION: sprawl = MANY agents on OVERLAPPING or unfocused work (the bad thing); DISJOINT sectors on non-overlapping files are the EXACT OPPOSITE -- the whole point of orchestrate-sectors -- and must be fired immediately in parallel. REFLEX before holding any delegation: list the target files of the running agents vs the new task; if the sets do NOT intersect, FIRE NOW with zero sprawl-hesitation. Opus hands are slow, so a pending disjoint sector left un-fired makes the whole job SLOWER -- the cost of NOT firing a safe parallel sector is real wall-clock loss. Do not over-correct into firing OVERLAPPING agents -- disjointness is the gate. Cross: claude-code-agent-tier-routing, foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore.

EMBODIED IN THE BUSY-FLEET GUARD DOOR (2026-06-27, user directive 'plant it in the harness guidance, in the busy-fleet default message'). The busy-fleet Block message (wkharness-common-tier.ps1 ~L175) now says: 'BETTER, don't tunnel ONE file serially: fan out the INDEPENDENT remaining work (handoff/Pending items in DISJOINT files) as PARALLEL background SECTORS, then spend the wait knowledge-ifying -- wkappbot skill read orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying.' WHY this placement: busy-fleet fires at the EXACT moment ROOT is about to do direct serial work (tunnel-vision), so the parallel-sector nudge lands at the door -- the foundation step-7 triple reflex (fix -> knowledge-ify -> EMBODY so it self-enforces). This catches the failure mode the predecessor + this session both hit: deep-serial on one hot-path file (git-guard) while independent handoff items (msgproto BOM, pace-DI dead-code, on-load compaction, dead-script detection) sat un-parallelized. WORKED EXAMPLE this session: 3 read-only investigation sectors (msgproto BOM=OK, pace-DI=WIRE-not-remove, on-load compaction) fanned out in ONE message while ROOT continued the git-guard CONNECT and knowledge-ified during the wait -- sectors must be DISJOINT files (collision-free) and read-only/proto deliverables (subagents are write-frozen on canonical + pace-blocked on PowerShell, so they investigate, ROOT applies). Cross: harness-busy-fleet-guard step 4 (idle-with-remaining-work = failure state), foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore step 7 (triple reflex), predicted-vs-actual-commando-calibration-ledger (pre-register EXPECT per sector).

RETIREMENT / HANDOFF FINISH via CONFLICT-AVOIDING PARALLEL-SECTOR DELEGATION (user 2026-06-28, do NOT serial-grind the OPEN items at retirement). When retiring with OPEN work, the successor must PARTITION the OPEN items into NON-CONFLICTING parallel SECTORS and DELEGATE them simultaneously, then supervise -- NOT serial-grind (which at over-pace burns ROOT budget + risks fatigue-errors on high-blast files). CONFLICT-AVOIDANCE RULE: each sector = a DISJOINT file/repo set so parallel agents NEVER edit the same source; when agents must mutate a shared file, use Agent isolation:worktree (each gets its own git worktree, auto-cleaned). The handoff OPEN list IS the sector menu -- pick sectors whose target FILES do not overlap. Example (2026-06-28 handoff): sector1=knowledge-chain-block (wkharness-anti-knowledge.ps1), sector2=committer-poison (wkharness-agent-name.ps1), sector3=installer forward-slash (wkharness-agy-install.ps1 + wkharness-codex-install.ps1) -- all DISJOINT canonical files -> safe to run in parallel. ROUTING per sector: a PRO + separate-pace executor edits canonical (codex once SEAM-E unblocks it, or agy-pro -- write-freeze allows pro, their own pace pool means Claude over-pace does not block them); CHEAP (Haiku) does read-only survey/verify only (never canonical code-write -- it drops chunks); ROOT supervises, promotes sandbox->canonical, commits. WHY parallel-disjoint beats serial: wall-clock = slowest-single-sector (not sum), and each agent spends ITS OWN pace not the ROOT's. The retiring ROOT names the sectors in the handoff; the successor fans them out. Cross: claude-session-handoff (the handoff names the sectors + their files), claude-code-agent-tier-routing (per-sector executor routing), foundation-is-roots-charge (ROOT orchestrates + supervises, does not grind).

2026-07-01: creating wkharness-claude-post.ps1 (Claude-dedicated PostToolUse entry, mirroring codex-main/agy-main's dedicated-family pattern) as one sector of the Claude-main/post/install family-dedicated-entry migration -- done in parallel with the claude-main copy while waiting on the codex/agy architecture survey.

LIVE 2026-07-02: study-lock re-blocked a re-dispatched Haiku (7 skills for wkharness-guards-write.ps1) even after ROOT had already read all 7 in-session -- study-lock is apparently PER-AGENT/PER-PROCESS, not session-wide, so each fresh subagent must independently satisfy its target file's study-lock, and ROOT reading the skills first does NOT pre-clear it for a delegate. Splitting the 15-Block()-pointer fix into 5 disjoint-file parallel sectors (matching busy-fleet's own suggestion) let each agent's smaller per-file skill set clear faster than one serial ROOT pass through all 5 files.
